A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Extra-CoT work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The latency and long-context material in v1 Appendices I–J can be matched to v3 Section 4.3.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, compressor-quality assessments, ablations, inference-latency measurements, and a human preference study.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in its main text and appendices, including benchmark performance and human preference measurements.

M1.justification: The question-aware Longformer compressor, formula-preserving supervision, mixed-ratio SFT, and CHRPO reward mechanism are unchanged. Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same procedures and objectives.

E1.justification: Both versions use CAMEL and MetaMathQA training material and evaluate GSM8K, MATH-500, AMC2023, SVAMP, MultiArith, MetaMath-1k, and MMLU STEM. No dataset, task, or evaluated population is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the base model, LC-Prompt, truncation, TokenSkip, and Thinkless/DeGRPO. LLMLingua-2 remains the compressor and human-study comparator, and the Pangu comparison retains both Auto and Fast presets.

E3.justification: The documented ratio grids, accuracy and think-only token metrics, context configurations, training schedules, and human-study design remain unchanged. Promoting the existing 16K evaluation into the main text does not introduce a new protocol; omission of its SFT-only qualification is a documentation loss, not evidence of changed execution.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the reward-component and fixed-SFT ablations, five-ratio versus endpoints-only comparison, OOD analysis, qualitative examples, compressor scoring, human study, and long-context evaluation. v3 summarizes or relocates existing analyses without adding a new test.

E5.justification: Both specify global seed 42 and retain the same human-vote aggregation. Neither introduces additional repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Matched tables and figures retain their result entries and values. For example, Table 1 still reports CHRPO at 64.8% accuracy and 452 tokens on MATH-500. v1 latency Table 7 and Pangu Table 8 become v3 Tables 5 and 4 with unchanged measurements; the expanded prose highlights existing comparisons.

T1.justification: Equations 1–12 retain the same compression definitions, losses, rewards, and difficulty score. The mathematical reasoning and monotonic teacher-budget criterion are unchanged, with no added theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same three-stage framework and extreme-compression claims, including over 73% token reduction with a 0.6-point accuracy improvement on MATH-500.

C2.justification: v3 more explicitly interprets cross-backbone gains as evidence for supervision quality and broadens the latency discussion from TokenSkip's observed behavior to low-fidelity compression generally. Its rewritten long-context discussion also omits v1 Appendix J's explicit restriction to SFT-stage results, weakening that qualification.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-availability statement and repository link to the abstract. Most implementation details remain unchanged, but the condensed long-context discussion drops the explicit SFT-only setup and explanations of the Auto and Fast presets previously supplied in Appendix J.

R1.justification: v3 adds Hu et al. (2026), 'From IDs to Semantics,' to the budget-aware reasoning citations. The Llama reference changes from Grattafiori et al. to Dubey et al. but identifies the same work. Overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Section 4.3 incorporates the former latency and long-context appendices and expands the summary of the existing human study. v3 also adds conflict-of-interest, funding, and impact statements and updates affiliations and publication text. Most scientific prose and the overall section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: The existing latency and Pangu tables move into the main text. The Pangu table is reformatted with baseline rows first, other tables and figures shift position, and the human-study caption moves below its table. The same seven figures and eight tables remain; no new visual evidence is introduced.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves accessibility and transparency by integrating existing latency and long-context evidence into Section 4.3, adding code-access information, and explicitly disclosing the Huawei relationship relevant to the Pangu evaluation. These gains are partly offset by losing the SFT-only qualification and preset descriptions from v1 Appendix J. The method and empirical evidence are unchanged, so the improvement is limited to presentation and documentation.
